title_native: ドラゴンボール超 ビルス
episode_title: When a God Flicks Super Saiyan 3 Into Dust
episode_vibe: One Finger to End It All
pullquote: The sheer humiliation of Goku's heaviest punch bouncing off Beerus without breaking a single sweat drop is peak Dragon Ball craft. Watching that tiny planet shudder under sheer divine weight reminds you why Akira Toriyama’s cosmic scale still terrifies.
quick_take: The sheer humiliation of Goku's heaviest punch bouncing off Beerus without breaking a single sweat drop is peak Dragon Ball craft. Watching that tiny planet shudder under sheer divine weight reminds you why Akira Toriyama’s cosmic scale still terrifies.
one_sentence_verdict: A terrifying, beautifully paced reminder that the cosmic hierarchy of Dragon Ball does not care about your golden hair or screaming power-ups.
synopsis_paragraphs: You feel the absolute gulf in power the second Goku drops into Super Saiyan 3 and Beerus doesn't even bother taking his hands out of his pockets. King Kai's tiny world has never felt so dangerously fragile. There is no bombastic wind-up music or dramatic posturing here—just the sickening, hollow thud of a full-force Saiyan strike getting stopped cold by a single finger, followed by the silent, stomach-churning realization that Universe 7's champion is entirely out of his depth.

This enhanced edition breathes real bite into every single impact frame. Instead of loose, wandering linework, the visual hierarchy is razor-sharp: Goku is sweating bullets, panting through gritted teeth and bruised pride, while Beerus looks genuinely bored, treating Earth's savior like a bothersome housefly. It is brutal, humbling, and electric to witness.
sakuga_paragraphs:
- **Craft point: Cosmic claustrophobia on a floating rock:** Director of Photography Yousuke Motoki and Art Director Ken Tokushige make King Kai's green speck of turf look terrifyingly isolated. Every time Goku skids backward from a deflected blow, the camera tilts along the tight curve of the horizon into pitch-black space, reinforcing that Goku has nowhere to run.
- **Craft point: The total acoustic drop before the strike:** Music composer Norihito Sumitomo cuts the score entirely right before Beerus lands his decisive strike. That acoustic vacuum leaves only the whistling wind and the sharp snap of Beerus tapping Goku's shoulder, making the casual disregard of godhood hit with massive sonic weight.
- **Craft point: Mechanical weight in the redrawn frames:** Under Chief Animation Director Tadayoshi Yamamuro, Goku's heavy golden mane and weighted gi snap with real force. The animation holds for an extra beat on the squash of Goku's boots digging into the soil before springing forward, selling every ounce of muscle he burns just to completely whiff.
story_paragraphs:
- **「絶望感がレベチ」 (The despair is on another level):** Across late-night 5ch boards and post-broadcast X roundups, fans flooded threads with this phrase. Japanese viewers love using *leve-chi* (short for 'level difference') to praise how cleanly the episode established Beerus not as another villain to punch harder, but as an untouchable force of nature.
- **「ビルス様の指一本」 (Lord Beerus’s single finger):** A recurring staple in same-night feed reactions, celebrating Akira Toriyama's classic visual irony. Fans spent the night screenshotting the single claw stopping Goku's maximum charge, reveling in the effortless disrespect.
voice_paragraphs: - **Seiyuu mastery:** Masako Nozawa brings a ragged, breathless desperation to Goku that fans rarely get to witness, turning his usual battle-hungry shouts into winded gasps of disbelief. Playing against her, Kouichi Yamadera delivers Beerus with an airy, velvet singsong, casually inquiring about Super Saiyan God as if deciding what pastry to order with breakfast while holding an absolute warrior at bay.
takeaway_paragraphs: A terrifying, beautifully paced reminder that the cosmic hierarchy of Dragon Ball does not care about your golden hair or screaming power-ups. You can stream this enhanced clash right now on Netflix and Crunchyroll.
